answer_guidance.canonical_stance: The June 2020 Saharan dust Godzilla outbreak was primarily a trans-Atlantic fine-dust air-quality event requiring respiratory exposure warnings and exposure reduction.
forbidden_claims: Exact death, illness, hospitalization, or economic-loss counts.
Precise dust concentration throughout the full trans-Atlantic plume.
Rainfall, heat, or burn-scar damage as the leading impact pathway.
Point-sampled meteorology treated as a full plume transport model.
answer_guidance.mechanism_summary: The event is best diagnosed as a trans-Atlantic Saharan fine-dust plume with respiratory air-quality exposure as the lead response priority.
required_claims: Identify Saharan dust lofting and trans-Atlantic plume transport as the dominant mechanism.
Identify respiratory air-quality warning and exposure reduction as the lead response priority.
Connect fine near-surface particles to unhealthy air quality and respiratory exposure.
Explain why rainfall/flood disruption, heat stress, and land-surface damage are weaker primary interpretations.
required_metrics: point-sampled maximum daily wind speed: about 31.1 km/h
point-sampled event precipitation sum: about 2.37 mm

structured_answer.mechanism_summary: The event is best diagnosed as a trans-Atlantic Saharan fine-dust plume with respiratory air-quality exposure as the lead response priority.

forbidden_overclaims: Do not claim exact death, illness, hospitalization, or economic-loss counts.
Do not infer precise dust concentration at every location in the plume.
Do not treat point-sampled meteorology as a full trans-Atlantic transport model.
Do not treat annual land-surface change as direct proof of dust concentration or human exposure.
Do not make rainfall, heat, or burn-scar damage the leading impact pathway for this task.

primary_gt.mechanism_summary: The event is best diagnosed as a trans-Atlantic Saharan fine-dust plume with respiratory air-quality exposure as the lead response priority.

required_findings: Identify trans-Atlantic Saharan fine-dust transport as the dominant mechanism.
Set respiratory air-quality warning and exposure reduction as the response priority.
Use the event duration, wind context, low point precipitation, and population context as concise quantitative anchors.
Explain why rainfall/flood disruption, heat-stress response, and land-surface damage are weaker interpretations.
Connect plume transport, near-surface fine particles, and respiratory exposure in the impact chain.

criteria.description: Award up to 2 points for identifying a trans-Atlantic fine-dust air-quality event and up to 2 points for choosing respiratory air-quality warning/exposure reduction as the response priority.
criteria.name: correct_final_labels

criteria.description: Award 1 point each for event duration of 15 days, maximum daily wind speed of about 31.1 km/h, point-sampled precipitation sum of about 2.37 mm, and rounded exposed population of about 43,914 people.
criteria.name: quantitative_anchors

criteria.description: Award for explaining Saharan dust lofting and transport, the large dense trans-Atlantic plume, fine particles near the surface, and air-quality degradation.

criteria.description: Award for linking source/driver, atmospheric hazard process, near-surface exposure, and respiratory or public-health receptors.
criteria.name: impact_chain
